newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leaders of the Liga Ng Mga Barangay (village) in Western Visayas are scheduled to meet on Monday in Iloilo City to discuss steps to speed up the signature campaign to amend the Constitution and extend the term of elected officials by two years. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Interior Secretary Robert Barbers has directed the Philippine National Police Traffic Management Group to patrol the North and South Luzon Expressways and curb the hijacking of trucks with export cargoes. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- More than 4,000 illegal immigrants from the Philippines have left the United Arab Emirates (UAE) under an unprecedented amnesty to escape criminal punishment, Philippine embassy officials in Abu Dhabi said. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Nur Misuari, governor of the Autonomous Region for Moslem Mindanao, said on Saturday he would ask Malacanang palace to give him powers to field a special task force of Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) fighters to go after kidnap-for-ransom gangs who operate outside the autonomous region. (MALAYA)
- Senator Gregorio "Gringo" Honasan favours extending the term of President Ramos because he doubts the credentials of those aspiring for the presidency in the 1998 elections. (MANILA STANDARD)
- Edgardo Espiritu, president of Westmont Bank, said he expected interest rates to continue to go down in the next few months. (TODAY)

- Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd Inc, the Malaysian firm which has got a majority stake in the formerly state-owned National Steel Corp, wants the Philippine government to hold on to its remaining 20 percent stake in the steel company. (TODAY)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is looking into reports the Philippine Stock Exchange abetted or even encouraged the takeover of inactive firms through so called "backdoor listing". (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
- The National Economic and Development Authority is confident the 7.5 percent to 8.7 percent inflation target this year will be achieved. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
